sections.h2: Red Willow County at a glance
sections.html:
Red Willow County runs along Nebraska's southern border, with McCook as the county seat. Indianola is the other city, and Bartley, Danbury and Lebanon are villages. Marion, Perry and Shippee are unincorporated. The Republican River crosses the north-central part, and the low ground along it is farmed.

The 2020 census counted 10,702 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 10,307, a drop of 3.7 percent. The count has slipped at every census since 1980. There are 4,532 households and 5,157 housing units, and 12.1% of those units were vacant. About 71.8% of occupied homes are owner-occupied.

After decades of slow loss, some owners would rather close quickly as-is than wait through a long listing. An empty house still gets a tax bill, and it ages faster when no one checks the roof, furnace and plumbing.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects the tax
sections.html:
Real estate tax is collected by the county treasurer at 502 Norris Avenue in McCook. Mail goes to PO Box 490, McCook, NE 69001, and the phone is 308-345-6515, extension 1. Current and back taxes can both be looked up and paid on the state's tax portal. Paying by card costs 2.35 percent with a $2.00 minimum, and an e-check costs $2.00.

The assessor is in the same building and can be reached at 308-345-4388 or assessor@redwillowcountyne.gov, weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., open through lunch. That office sets values on real and personal property, keeps the parcel maps, builds the tax roll the treasurer works from, and answers questions about homestead exemption eligibility.

The assessor names four things that move a value: changes in the market, outside influences on the property, adding or removing improvements, and a remodel or rehab. A new garage or finished basement pushes the number up, and tearing down an old outbuilding should bring it down.

Exemptions exist for educational and religious facilities and for qualifying seniors and people with disabilities. Ask the assessor's office which one applies before you assume you are paying the full amount.

Get the protest to the County Clerk on or before June 30. It must state the value you are asking for and your reasons. The clerk mails the board's decision by August 2, and you have until August 24 to take it to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission.

Back your number with evidence. A recent appraisal, photos and a bid for needed repairs, or sale prices of similar houses give the board something concrete to work with.

sections.h2: How the March tax sale works
sections.html:
Each year on the first Monday in March, the county sells certificates for unpaid real estate tax in the courthouse. The delinquent list runs in the local paper and online for three consecutive weeks in February.

  • A buyer purchases the delinquent tax, not the property, and pays later years' taxes as they come due.
  • The owner has a three-year redemption period, and the certificate earns 14 percent interest.
  • If the owner has not redeemed after three years, the certificate holder has six months to foreclose.
  • Registration for buyers costs $25, and the county charges $20 for each certificate sold.

The treasurer will not give legal advice to certificate buyers and refers them to Nebraska statutes 77-1801 through 77-1941. An owner facing a sale on a parcel should talk with an attorney, and should not wait for the final week.

At closing the title company asks the treasurer for the payoff, takes it from your proceeds and records the deed. If the parcel has already gone to the March sale, the certificate has to be redeemed first, so ask the treasurer whether one exists before you set a date.

The seller also pays Nebraska's documentary stamp tax through the register of deeds, at $3.32 for each $1,000 of value for deeds recorded from July 18, 2026.

A cash sale avoids the lender's appraisal and repair demands, which helps with an older or vacant house. Send us the parcel number and we can go through the numbers with you.

Bring your parcel number, a photo ID and your latest tax statement when you call or visit. For an inherited house, bring papers that show who is allowed to sign. If the house is empty, tell the title company early, since an unoccupied property may need extra care before closing.

faqs.q: When do Red Willow County taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: The first half turns delinquent May 1 and the second half September 1.

faqs.q: How do I protest my Red Willow County valuation?
faqs.a: Send your protest to the County Clerk on or before June 30, with the value you want and your reasons. The Board of Equalization hears it, and its decision can be appealed to the state commission.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Red Willow County valuation?
faqs.a: Call the assessor at 308-345-4388. The office is at 502 Norris Avenue in McCook and is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I pay Red Willow County property tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes, on the tax portal, for a 2.35 percent fee with a $2.00 minimum. An e-check costs $2.00, and you can mail a payment to PO Box 490, McCook.

faqs.q: What is the Red Willow County tax sale?
faqs.a: It is the yearly sale of certificates for unpaid real estate tax, held the first Monday in March. Certificates carry 14 percent interest, with a three-year redemption period.
